messages:
maria: Hey team — onboarding antlia-7b. I pulled the HF snapshot but the s3 mirror checksum doesn't match. HF hash: b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184, S3 reported an ETag a3f5e7... Anyone else seeing this?
jon: Did you use the mirror job or manual copy? Which exact S3 path?
maria: Mirror job. Path: s3://redwood-artifacts/models/antlia-7b/2024-11-01/weights.bin
sam: can you paste the exact sha256 you computed locally? I can compare with the registry.
maria: local sha256: b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184
lee: Registry's release tag v1.0 shows that same sha256 for the HF release. Note: S3 ETag is not reliable for multipart uploads, so mismatch is expected if upload was multipart.
infra-bot: FYI: s3 multipart uploads produce ETag that's not the sha256. Use `aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-artifacts --key models/antlia-7b/2024-11-01/weights.bin --query ChecksumSHA256` if we enabled server-side checksums.
jon: ^ exactly. Our mirroring job currently doesn't set ChecksumSHA256 metadata or emit a manifest. That's the gap.
maria: is there a quick fix? I can re-run a copy with different flags. I previously used `aws s3 cp weights.bin s3://... --metadata-directive REPLACE`.
sam: short-term workaround: add a manifest next to the object with canonical sha256 and tokenizer info. e.g. create `s3://redwood-artifacts/models/antlia-7b/v1/manifest.json` with:
```
{"sha256":"b1946ac92492d2347c6235b4d2611184","size":"123456789","tokenizer":"hf/antlia-tokenizer@v1"}
```
That lets registry verification be deterministic.
maria: I'll put that up now. Do we also need a registry update? It currently points at hf://redwood/antlia-7b v1 and the s3 mirror path.
lee: Yes — file a PR to artifact-registry (or push via the internal submit form) to mark the s3 path as verified and include the checksum. Also set the object ACL to private and ensure lifecycle rules are appropriate (we usually avoid GLACIER for actively served models).
jon: For reproducibility, this is the command we use internally to compute sha256 from S3 (note it's slow for large files):
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-artifacts/models/antlia-7b/2024-11-01/weights.bin - | sha256sum
```
If the upload used server-side checksum metadata it's better to query head-object.
sam: I'll propose a longer-term fix: small lambda/worker that runs after mirror copy to compute sha256 and write ChecksumSHA256 metadata or a manifest. Created infra issue #412 to track.
maria: uploaded manifest and pushed registry submit link: https://internal/redwood/artifacts/submit with payload.
lee: I reviewed and accepted the PR in artifact-registry; added `checksum` field to the entry referencing the manifest. infra issue: https://github.com/redwood/infra/issues/412
jon: One more item — tokenizer quirk: antlia tokenizer v1 lowercases special token `|ENT|` in some tokenizers; our evals are failing. Maria, please include tokenizer_version and a short note in the manifest so QA knows.
maria: done. manifest now contains `tokenizer_version: v1-lc` and note `special_tokens: ["|ENT|"] lowercased`.
deploy-bot: mirroring job rerun scheduled at 2024-11-02T03:00Z (job id: mirror-20241102-03).
sam: great. Close the loop: maria, can you confirm the model loads on dedicated staging and run a quick smoke inference? If green we'll flip registry flag to `ready-to-serve`.
maria: Loading on staging now, will post result.
maria: Staging load OK, sample inference passes. Marking registry flag to ready and closing loop. :tada:
